aiOverview.content: Response to Intervention (RTI) is a multi-tier educational framework used to identify and support students struggling with learning or behavior through early intervention and data-driven instruction. It provides increasingly intense, research-based interventions to improve student outcomes, often within a General Education setting. Key Components of RTI: Universal Screening: Identifying all students at risk early. Multi-Tiered System: Tier 1: High-quality, differentiated classroom instruction for all students. Tier 2: Targeted, small-group interventions for students not making sufficient progress. Tier 3: Intensive, individualized interventions or specialized instruction. Progress Monitoring: Continuously tracking student data to measure growth and adjust instruction. Data-Based Decision Making: Using data to determine if a student needs higher-level support or specialized evaluation. Key Differences: RTI vs. Special Education: RTI is a general education initiative designed for all students; it is not, itself, a special education program, though it can be used to identify students needing special education evaluations. Goal: The goal is to provide immediate support to prevent long-term failure and bridge learning gaps. Other Meanings: RTI International: A non-profit research institute. Real-Time Innovations (RTI): A software framework company for autonomous systems. Respiratory Tract Infection (RTI): An infectious disease.
